messages.subject: HMM implementation
parts:
Hi to ALL!

I´m working with the Affymetrix 5.0 and I´m running aroma to process
my chips. My boss doesn´t want to use a segmentation algorithm like
CBS or GLAD instead he´d rather prefer and HMM option, like CNAT for
10k to 500k.

I wonder if you know something like CNAT for Affy 5.0 or should I have
to implement by myself ?

If I have to program the HMM, how could I use the results generated by
aroma?

Thanks in advance!

David

On Thu, Apr 16, 2009 at 11:53 AM, David <daesc...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi to ALL!
>
> I´m working with the Affymetrix 5.0 and I´m running aroma to process
> my chips. My boss doesn´t  want to use a segmentation algorithm like
> CBS or GLAD instead he´d rather prefer and HMM option, like CNAT for
> 10k  to 500k.
>
> I wonder if you know something like CNAT for Affy 5.0 or should I have
> to implement by myself ?

It's not implemented, i.e. there are no wrappers providing that.

Note that CNAT was designed for 100K & 500K arrays, and that
Affymetrix does not provide software for CN analysis on
GenomeWideSNP_5 (it is targeted as a genotyping chip type not a CN
one).

>
> If I have to program the HMM, how could I use the results generated by
> aroma?

If you think you're up for it, in the latest release, we moved one
step closer to provide plugins for existing segmentation methods. All
this new code is currently in the aroma.core package (part of the
installation). Have a look at:

library("aroma.core");
example(segmentByCBS.RawGenomicSignals)

for an illustration. Then look at the code of segmentByCBS() for the
RawGenomicSignals class, i.e.

print(segmentByCBS.RawGenomicSignals)

If you can setup a segmentByMyHMM.RawGenomicSignals function that
works with the above example, then you're almost done. Then it is a
matter of a few lines of code by me for having it running on
Affymetrix data.

...the alternative is to convince your boss that CBS is working really
well for segmentation problems.

/Henrik
